verdict.rationale: Snyk Studio documents a default hooks-based integration for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot, designed so code written by AI coding assistants is "secure at inception". It also ships an official local MCP server, backed by the Snyk CLI, that a coding agent can call to scan the directory, plus /snyk-fix commands inside the assistant. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the hooks actually gate AI-generated code before it lands, detailed docs on hook behavior (blocking vs. advisory), and hooks cover only "some" agentic environments.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can wire the scanner into my coding agent so AI-generated code is scanned for issues before it lands

citations.quote: Snyk Studio supports a default hooks-based approach for some agentic development environments (ADEs) to ensure code written by AI coding assistants is secure at inception (SAI): Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot
The Snyk MCP Server is designed as a local MCP server, running on your system using the Snyk CLI to ensure local file access.
To validate the MCP server configuration, prompt your coding agent with natural language, for example, "scan my directory for security issues".
Run `/snyk-fix` in your coding assistant to scan the project and apply a fix for the top vulnerability.
